text: What if your cat doubled in size and never stopped?
formula: title question, spoken word for word (STANDARD 1.3)

text: It's dinner time. Mittens is hungry. You stay on the couch.
formula: stake/thread: Mittens wants dinner, the hero stays on the couch. Start height h0 = 0.30 m (house cat standing, top of head); start weight w0 = 4 kg (typical adult house cat ~4-5 kg). h(1) = 0.6 m, w(1) = 32 kg

text: Real cats stop growing after about a year. Mittens just doubled.
formula: reality first: most cats reach adult size at about 12 months (PetMD, Catster; big breeds later). h(2) = 0.30 m x 2^2 = 1.2 m; w(2) = 4 kg x 8^2 = 256 kg. Label: longest domestic cat ever, Stewie (Maine Coon), 123 cm nose to tail (Guinness 2010, Wikipedia)

text: Twice as tall, wide and long means eight times heavier. Bye, couch.
formula: square-cube law: weight scales with length^3 -> 2 x 2 x 2 = 8x per doubling. h(n) = 0.30 m x 2^n, w(n) = 4 kg x 8^n. n=3: 2.4 m, 4 x 512 = 2,048 kg ~ 2 t (heavier than a typical car, ~1.5 t) -> the couch she sits on is flattened. Joke set up in n1 (the couch)

text: Almost five metres. She doesn't fit, so the roof comes off.
formula: h(4) = 0.3 x 16 = 4.8 m > a one-storey cottage (ceiling 2.6 m, ridge ~4.6 m); w(4) = 4 x 4,096 = 16,384 kg ~ 16 t

text: Nearly ten metres. Your neighbour walks past with a birthday cake.
formula: h(5) = 0.3 x 32 = 9.6 m; w(5) = 4 x 32,768 = 131,072 kg ~ 131 t (a blue whale: up to ~150 t, NOAA/Britannica)

text: Thirty-eight metres. Mittens found her dinner. It was the cake.
A hundred and fifty metres. All because you stayed on the couch.
formula: h(9) = 0.3 x 512 = 153.6 m (taller than the Great Pyramid, 146.6 m originally); w(9) = 4 x 8^9 = 536,870,912 kg ~ 537,000 t. Blame set up in n1

text: Over a kilometre. Taller than any building. Her ears are in the clouds.
formula: h(12) = 0.3 x 4,096 = 1,228.8 m > Burj Khalifa 828 m (tallest building); low cloud bases ~0.5-2 km; w(12) = 4 x 8^12 = 2.75e11 kg = 275 million t

text: Almost ten kilometres. Taller than Everest. Planes fly around her.
formula: h(15) = 0.3 x 32,768 = 9,830 m > Mount Everest 8,849 m; airliners cruise at ~10-12 km; w(15) = 4 x 8^15 = 1.41e14 kg

text: A hundred and fifty kilometres. No air up there. Nobody hears her meow.
formula: h(19) = 0.3 x 524,288 = 157,286 m ~ 157 km > Karman line (100 km, where space begins); sound needs air to travel, and there is almost none above 100 km

text: Forty thousand kilometres. Now she's heavier than the whole Earth.
formula: h(27) = 0.3 x 2^27 = 40,265 km (more than Earth's circumference, 40,075 km; ~3.2 Earth diameters of 12,742 km); w(27) = 4 x 8^27 = 4 x 2^81 = 9.67e24 kg > Earth's mass 5.97e24 kg

text: Thirty-one doublings. Her head is past the Moon.
formula: h(31) = 0.3 x 2^31 = 644,245 km > Earth-Moon distance 384,400 km

text: And she still wants her dinner.
formula: punchline: pays off the stake from n1 (dinner)

text: What should we try next? Tell us in the comments.
formula: ending ask over the last shot (STANDARD 1.9)
